credit.credit-words: "Ellipsis" or "elliptic progression" (in music theory) is a phenomenon similar to an interrupted cadence, when the
expected functional resolution of a chord is skipped, and the first chord is connected to an unexpected chord,
often dissonant and belonging to a different key. Rimsky-Korsakov and Tchaikovsky use the term
"false progression". And Georgy Catoire introduced the term "ellipsis", which is firmly entrenched in the
In elliptical progression may enter different types of chords (triads, seventh chords, ninth chords...).
In this collection shows examples of connections of dominant seventh chords.
